title: Hub GCSE History Topic Checklist (Aligned to Edexcel 1HI0)
subtitle: Option B3: Henry VIII and his ministers, 1509–40

exam_structure.overview: Tests British depth across 3 Key Topics. Q1(a)/(b) Describe features (4m), Q2 Explain why causation (12m), Q3/Q4 Choice essay with stimulus points (16m).

sections.title: Key topic 1: Henry VIII and Wolsey, 1509–29

topics.title: 1. Henry VIII, Renaissance Prince
points: England in 1509: society & government; young Henry & his accession to the throne
Henry’s character & views on sovereignty & monarchy; His personal style of government
Strengths, weaknesses & aims as monarch

topics.title: 2. The rise of Wolsey and his policies
points: Causes of Wolsey’s rise to power; His personality, roles & wealth
Wolsey’s reforms: enclosures, finance & justice; The Eltham Ordinances
Causes of & reactions to the Amicable Grant

topics.title: 3. Wolsey’s foreign policy
points: Aims of Wolsey’s foreign policy
Successes & failures (incl. relations with France & the Holy Roman Empire, the Treaty of London (1518), the ‘Field of the Cloth of Gold’ (1520) & increasing difficulties in the 1520s)

topics.title: 4. Wolsey, Catherine, the succession and annulment
points: Catherine of Aragon & the succession
Henry’s reasons for & attempts to gain an annulment; Opposition to the annulment (incl. Pope Clement VII)
Causes of Wolsey’s fall from power (incl. the failure of the divorce proceedings in London & t he influence of the Boleyns)

sections.title: Key topic 2: Henry VIII and Cromwell, 1529–40

topics.title: 1. Cromwell’s rise to power, 1529–34
points: Personality & early career (incl. service to Wolsey, election as MP & eventual membership of the Royal Council)
Handling of the king’s annulment & influence over Henry; Role as the king’s Chief Minister

topics.title: 2. T he king’s marriages
points: Causes of fall of Anne Boleyn (incl. Cromwell)
Causes of marriage to Jane Seymour; her influence, heir & death
Causes of marriage to Anne of Cleves

topics.title: 3. Cromwell and government, 1534–40
points: Reform of government & royal finance
Management & use of parliament

topics.title: 4. The fall of Cromwell
points: Causes of Cromwell’s fall from power in 1540 (incl. Duke of Norfolk & the failure of the marriage to Anne of Cleves)

sections.title: Key topic 3: The Reformation and its impact, 1529–40

topics.title: 1. The break with Rome
points: Henry as ‘Defender of the Faith’; Causes of Henry’s campaign against the Pope & the Catholic Church, 1529–33
Significance: Act of Succession & the Act of Supremacy (1534) for the break with Rome; Cromwell’s role in their enforcement (incl. oaths & treason laws)

topics.title: 2. Opposition to, and impact of, Reformation, 1534–40
points: Elizabeth Barton (the Nun of Kent) & John Fisher
Significance: opposition from Thomas More
Impact of the Reformation on the English Church (incl. Thomas Cranmer & the influence of Thomas Cromwell)

topics.title: 3. The dissolution of the monasteries
points: Religious houses in local communities
Causes of dissolutions (incl. the findings of Cromwell’s commissions of 1535)
Impact of the dissolutions; Beneficiaries & losers

topics.title: 4. The Pilgrimage of Grace, 1536
points: Causes of uprising
Key events of the uprising (incl. rebellions in Lincolnshire & Yorkshire & the roles of Robert Aske & the Duke of Norfolk)
